title: gulf stocks fall after us iran exchange strikes 2026 09 02
text:
BENGALURU, Sept 2 (Reuters) - Gulf stock markets fell on Wednesday after the U.S. and Iran exchanged strikes overnight, dimming hopes for ​a swift easing of tensions in the Middle East.
Iran and its Arab neighbours ‌were drawn back into conflict after U.S. forces struck Iran's southern coast and Tehran fired at American bases across the region, in the largest exchange of fire between Washington and Tehran since July.
Qatar's benchmark (.QSI)
, opens new tab
 dropped 1%, with nearly ​all stocks trading lower. Industries Qatar (IQCD.QA)
, opens new tab
 fell 1.5%, while Qatar National Bank (QNBK.QA)
, opens new tab
, the region's ​largest lender, lost 1.4%.
Saudi Arabia's benchmark index (.TASI)
, opens new tab
 declined 0.8%, led by information ⁠technology, communications and healthcare shares. Saudi National Bank (1180.SE)
, opens new tab
, the kingdom's largest lender by assets, fell ​1.6%, while Dar Al Arkan Real Estate Development (4300.SE)
, opens new tab
 dropped 5.4%.
Electrical Industries (1303.SE)
, opens new tab
 and East Pipes Integrated Company ​for Industry (1321.SE)
, opens new tab
 bucked the broader trend, rising 2.4% and 4.8%, respectively.
Separately, Saudi Arabia raised $3.25 billion through a two-tranche U.S. dollar sukuk sale, its second debt-market transaction this year, IFR reported. Orders exceeded $15 billion, with proceeds earmarked for general budgetary ​needs.
Abu Dhabi's benchmark index (.FTFADGI)
, opens new tab
 fell 0.7%, weighed down by consumer discretionary, telecommunications and real estate ​stocks. ADNOC Gas (ADNOCGAS.AD)
, opens new tab
 lost 1.2%, while conglomerate Alpha Dhabi Holding (ALPHADHABI.AD)
, opens new tab
 declined 2.8%.
Dubai's main index (.DFMGI)
, opens new tab
 slipped 0.3%, with most ‌constituents posting ⁠declines. Blue-chip developer Emaar Properties (EMAR.DU)
, opens new tab
 fell 1.7%, while toll-road operator Salik (SALIK.DU)
, opens new tab
 dropped 1.5%.
"Geopolitical developments are likely to continue to affect investor sentiment as traders closely monitor oil prices, shipping conditions in the Strait of Hormuz and progress in diplomatic efforts," said Andrei Constantin, commercial director and trading ​adviser at TFP Software ​FZCO.
"A reduction in regional ⁠risk could support local markets, while a sustained escalation may keep a cautious tone across GCC equity markets," he said.
Outside the Gulf, Egypt's blue-chip ​index (.EGX30)
, opens new tab
 rose 0.5%, supported by materials, industrial and consumer discretionary shares. ​Misr Fertilizers Production ⁠Company (MFPC.CA)
, opens new tab
 climbed 9%, while Abu Qir Fertilizers and Chemical Industries (ABUK.CA)
, opens new tab
 rose 6.8%.
Egypt expects the Damietta regasification vessel, which was damaged in a drone attack in July, to resume operations in the fourth quarter of ⁠the ​year.
